backlog.spec: Replace the binary Morgan bit vector with the hashed count vector: use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(...).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy(mol) with the same radius 2 and 2048 bits. Everything else (RandomForest settings, seed handling) stays the same. Counts keep how many times each substructure occurs, which often helps on logD-type targets.
backlog.title: Morgan count fingerprints

backlog.spec: In featurize, compute Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors(mol) for each molecule (a dict of about 200 RDKit descriptors such as MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3). Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip extreme values to a sane range. Hstack these with the Morgan features before fitting the RandomForest. Descriptors like MolLogP and TPSA carry most of the signal for lipophilicity.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a small block of counts of ionizable groups computed with RDKit SMARTS patterns: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, phenol, aliphatic amine (primary, secondary, tertiary), amidine/guanidine, pyridine-type basic N, sulfonic acid, and quaternary nitrogen. logD at pH 7.4 depends strongly on ionization, so these counts are appended to the Morgan features. Keep the list to about 10 patterns.
backlog.title: Ionization-state SMARTS features

backlog.spec: Before computing any features, keep only the largest covalent fragment (Chem.rdmolops.GetMolFrags with asMols, pick the heaviest) and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. Apply the same cleaning to train and test SMILES. This removes counterion and salt effects so that the same parent compound gets one consistent representation.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurizing

backlog.spec: Swap the ECFP-style atom invariants for pharmacophoric ones: create the generator with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=2, fpSize=2048, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Use the count fingerprint. Feature-based atom classes (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) generalize better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: FCFP feature-invariant Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add a second fingerprint block using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024) and GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator(fpSize=1024), both as count vectors. Concatenate them with the Morgan counts. Atom pairs capture long-range shape and size, which complements the local circular environments of Morgan.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys from rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol) to the feature matrix as a fixed set of interpretable substructure bits. Use them alongside Morgan counts. MACCS is a small, dense feature set that tree models can use efficiently.
backlog.title: MACCS structural keys

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan generator to radius 3 with 4096 bits, using count fingerprints. Keep the RandomForest unchanged. Larger radius captures bigger fragments, and the extra bits reduce hash collisions. This is a single-parameter change to the featurizer settings.
backlog.title: Radius and bit-size sweep for Morgan

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor(objective='l1', n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.5, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed). Train on the same Morgan count features. An L1 objective directly matches the MAE scoring.
backlog.title: LightGBM regressor with MAE objective

backlog.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor(loss_function='MAE', iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the concatenation of Morgan counts and RDKit descriptors. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees often generalize well on small tabular chemistry data. Keep the total fit time within the budget.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss on fingerprint and descriptor features

backlog.spec: Use sklearn.ensemble.HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='absolute_error', max_iter=600, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=seed) on the descriptor plus fingerprint matrix. It is fast on 2000-plus dense features and optimizes the MAE directly.
backlog.title: Histogram gradient boosting with absolute-error loss

backlog.spec: Compute a Tanimoto (MinMax for counts) similarity kernel over the Morgan count vectors: K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)). Fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1) on the train-by-train kernel and predict with the test-by-train kernel. Chemical similarity kernels are a strong baseline for fingerprint regression and extrapolate sensibly to new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Use the same Tanimoto kernel on Morgan count vectors and fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.5) to the training targets, centering y by its mean first and adding the mean back at prediction time. Kernel ridge with a chemistry kernel is a smooth alternative to SVR and has a single regularization knob.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process-style kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, find the k=10 most similar training molecules by Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bit vectors and predict the similarity-weighted mean of their targets (weights = similarity to the power 3). Use the full training set to compute similarities. This nonparametric predictor is a useful diverse member for blending.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour regression

backlog.spec: Train three base models on the same features: the existing RandomForest, a LightGBM with l1 objective, and the Tanimoto-kernel SVR. Predict on the test set with each model and return the arithmetic mean of the three prediction vectors. Averaging diverse models usually lowers MAE more than any single one, and the fits are independent so they can run in sequence within the time limit.
backlog.title: Simple averaged ensemble of RF, LightGBM and SVR

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold inner KFold on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from base models (RandomForest, LightGBM l1, Tanimoto SVR). Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression with positive=True) on those out-of-fold predictions to find blending weights. Then refit each base model on all training data and blend their test predictions with those weights. Keep the number of base models small so the total runtime stays under the budget.
backlog.title: Stacking with a ridge meta-learner over inner out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor fit with squared error for speed, but instead of the mean, return the median of the individual tree predictions for each test molecule (np.median over the per-tree outputs from estimators_). Since the metric is MAE, the median of the tree ensemble is a more robust central estimate when the label distribution has outliers.
backlog.title: Random forest with MAE-friendly leaf median prediction

backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES to 1000 and set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 2 and MAX_FEATURES to 0.2. Keep the Morgan bit features. A bigger forest reduces variance, and a slightly larger leaf size regularizes the fit. Check the job time, which should stay well under the 10-minute limit for all 15 fits.
backlog.title: Larger forest with tuned leaf size

backlog.spec: Set max_features='sqrt' and bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7 on the RandomForestRegressor, keeping 500 trees. Subsampling rows and features more aggressively decorrelates trees, which often helps when fingerprint features are highly redundant.
backlog.title: Random forest with sqrt feature sampling and bootstrap fraction

backlog.spec: In the LightGBM model, set bagging_fraction (subsample) to 0.7 with bagging_freq=1, feature_fraction (colsample_bytree) to 0.4, and min_child_samples=20 with reg_lambda=1.0. Use the l1 objective. Smaller mini-batches of rows per tree act as a regularizer on this small dataset (about 3000 molecules).
backlog.title: LightGBM with row and feature bagging

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, hold out 10 percent of the training molecules (stratified by target quantile, seeded) as a validation set. Train LightGBM with objective 'l1', learning_rate 0.05 and up to 3000 trees, using early_stopping(100) on the validation L1. Then retrain on all training molecules with the best iteration count scaled by 1.1. Early stopping prevents overfitting without manual tuning of n_estimators.
backlog.title: Learning-rate schedule with inner early stopping for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with a learning-rate schedule that decays over iterations: pass learning_rates=lambda i: 0.1 * (0.995 ** i) (or a piecewise schedule dropping from 0.1 to 0.02 at 500 iterations) to lgb.train with objective 'l1'. Early high learning rate fits the broad trend quickly, and later small steps refine it with less noise.
backlog.title: Decaying shrinkage schedule for boosting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to the 1st and 99th percentile of the training targets (np.clip with np.percentile). Predict on the unclipped scale. Logd measurement outliers can distort tree leaves and the kernel fits, and clipping keeps only the bulk of the distribution, which lowers the MAE on the typical molecule.
backlog.title: Winsorize extreme training targets

backlog.spec: Apply sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200) fitted on the training descriptor matrix (RDKit physchem descriptors) before feeding SVR, kernel ridge or MLP models. Heavy-tailed descriptors such as MolWt and counts get mapped to a well-scaled range, which these models need. Tree models stay on the raw features.
backlog.title: Quantile-transform descriptors for kernel and neural models

backlog.spec: Train sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), alpha=1e-3, learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.1, max_iter=300, random_state=seed) on log1p-scaled Morgan count features. Average 5 MLPs with seeds derived from the seed argument. The network captures smooth additive effects that trees miss, and averaging reduces variance.
backlog.title: Ensemble of seed-varied MLP on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build a small torch-free MLP in numpy or via sklearn MLPRegressor with solver='adam', alpha=1e-2 (L2 weight decay), and batch_size=64, training on Morgan count features plus RDKit descriptors scaled with StandardScaler. Use a fixed number of epochs (about 200) and no early stopping, so the training schedule is deterministic given the seed. Strong weight decay limits overfitting on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Adam-trained MLP with dropout-like regularization

backlog.spec: Compute each training molecule's density as the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 10 nearest training neighbours. Set sample weight = 1 / (density + 0.1) normalized to mean 1 and pass it to the RandomForest fit (sample_weight argument). This down-weights molecules in dense chemical clusters so that sparse regions influence the model more, which helps generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Inverse-density sample weighting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make an inner 5-fold out-of-fold prediction on the training set with the base model, fit a linear map y = a*pred + b that minimizes absolute error (use scipy.optimize.minimize on mean absolute residual or an L1 linear regression), and apply the map to the test predictions. Tree ensembles shrink predictions toward the mean, and this step expands them back to the correct spread.
backlog.title: Post-hoc linear recalibration of predictions

backlog.spec: For each molecule, compute the generic Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric) and its Morgan count fingerprint at radius 2, and append these 1024 bits to the feature matrix. Because test molecules come from unseen skeletons, the generic scaffold shape carries information that generalizes across the held-out folds even when the exact scaffold is absent in training.
backlog.title: Scaffold-generic fingerprints as extra features

backlog.spec: Add counts of common functional-group fragments from RDKit's fragment descriptors (rdkit.Chem.Fragments, functions fr_* such as fr_COO, fr_NH2, fr_halogen, fr_sulfonamd, fr_ether) to the feature matrix. These are about 85 interpretable integer counts. Trees use them to pick up group contributions to lipophilicity directly, without relying on fingerprint hashing.
backlog.title: Mordred-style fragment count features

incumbent.description: Adds a CatBoost regressor (MAE loss, 1000 iterations, depth 6) on Morgan count fingerprints concatenated with the RDKit descriptors as a fourth member, averaged equally with the RF, SVR and LightGBM predictions.

memo: Helped: richer features and more diverse ensemble members. Quantile-transformed RDKit descriptors gave the biggest gain (0.6304, -0.0926). MACCS keys gave -0.0090. A LightGBM L1 member gave -0.0116. Atom-pair/torsion count fingerprints gave -0.0091. Ionizable-group SMARTS counts gave -0.0135 (0.5872). A CatBoost MAE member on Morgan counts gave -0.0192, reaching the incumbent 0.5679. Did not help: bigger RF (+0.0018), Morgan radius 3 / 4096 bits (-0.0001, within noise), removing the nested stacking loop (-0.0015), and the stacker crashed. The recalibration attempt was aborted. Noise sd is about 0.0042, so gains under about 0.005 are unreliable. Next: add more chemistry-specific features (more SMARTS, charge/pKa-like descriptors); try an XGBoost member or a second CatBoost on different features; tune ensemble weights simply; recheck the LightGBM-for-RF swap (0.6007/0.6038) on the current ensemble with replicates; avoid more RF tuning and fingerprint widening.
